Class DemoDataRunner

java.lang.Object
de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.service.demo.DemoDataRunner
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.boot.CommandLineRunner
@Component @Profile("demo") @Order(100) public class DemoDataRunner extends Object implements org.springframework.boot.CommandLineRunner
Hangs the demo data set into startup without the platform having to know it exists.

Why a separate class rather than letting DemoDataService implement the runner: seed() is @Transactional, and a runner calling its own seed() would be an internal call — the proxy would not intercept it and the whole data set would be written without a transaction. Going through the injected bean keeps the proxy in the path.

Ordering: the demo data builds on what InitializationService creates (the admin account it acts as, above all), so it must run second. Both runners therefore carry an explicit Order; an unordered bean sorts as lowest precedence, which would silently put this one first.

peter haller
